claim: The huge difference in processing speed between AI and human brains may imply that parallel processing of data is sufficient for AI to accomplish tasks that require integrated (conscious) processes in humans.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing AI performance on tasks that are thought to require consciousness in humans and assessing whether parallel processing alone accounts for the performance.

conditions: AI processes much more data in a much faster way than human brains
exclusions: limited to the interpreted argument; no direct experimental support

title: High processing speed–sufficiency for tasks requiring principle

claim: Aggregation methods that incorporate verbalized confidence (e.g., Pair-Rank, Avg-Conf) outperform consistency-only aggregation, especially when LLM queries are costly and sampling frequency is limited.
falsifier: One can compare aggregation methods with and without verbalized confidence under varying query cost constraints and measure performance.

conditions: especially when LLM queries are costly and sampling frequency is limited
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported aggregation methods, models, and tasks; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Aggregation method incorporating verbalized for effectiveness

claim: The O(3,2) group can be contracted to the inhomogeneous Lorentz group, which serves as the basic space-time symmetry for quantum mechanics in a Lorentz-covariant world.
falsifier: One can verify the contraction by applying the group contraction procedure to the O(3,2) algebra and confirming that the resulting commutation relations match those of the inhomogeneous Lorentz group.

exclusions: limited to the reported system and experimental conditions

title: Group theory–inhomogeneous Lorentz group as theorem
